# Spheron Network

Spheron Network is a Technology, Information and Internet company. Spheron is an enterprise GPU rental company that offers on-demand rental of NVIDIA H100, A100, B200, and AMD MI300X GPUs. They provide fast deployment from Tier 3/4 data centers and offer AI training and LLM inference. Spheron Network employs 8 people (-50.0% YoY, -8 people), founded in 2020. Headquartered in Bengaluru, Karnataka, India, with presence in United States and Israel. Its workforce is distributed across India, United States, and Nigeria.

## About

Spheron is a unified GPU cloud marketplace that gives AI teams access to H100s, B200s, B300s, and more, across multiple data center providers, from a single dashboard.
We cut through hyperscaler pricing. Our H100s start at $2.00/hr (vs $4.76/hr on AWS), with no contracts, per-minute billing, and GPUs ready in under 90 seconds. Teams get full root SSH access, dedicated IPs, and Docker/Kubernetes support on Tier 2-4 compliant infrastructure with 99.9% uptime SLA.
What we solve: AI startups and enterprises waste months on GPU procurement and overpay 2-5x on AWS, GCP, and Azure. Spheron gives them one account, one bill, and the freedom to deploy on whichever provider has the best price without rewriting a single line of code.
Use cases: LLM training and fine-tuning, production inference serving, generative AI, distributed training with InfiniBand, and research workloads.
Start building: https://app.spheron.network

- [2026-11-08 · Posted] [Buying more GPUs will not fix a slow chatbot. Reusing what you...](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/spheron_buying-more-gpus-will-not-fix-a-slow-chatbot-activity-7525053351001186304-_01J)
  > Buying more GPUs will not fix a slow chatbot. Reusing what you already computed does.
  >
  > On Llama 3.1 70B, a 128K-token system prompt takes 11.2 seconds to reach the first output token when every node reads it cold. Share that memory across nodes with LMCache instead, and the same prompt drops to 1.5 seconds. Both numbers are from Spheron's own benchmark.
  >
  > A KV cache is the memory a model builds while reading your prompt, so it never rereads the same words. Each node normally keeps its own copy and starts from zero.
  >
  > LMCache lets nodes running vLLM, the open source inference server, share that cache instead of each rebuilding it alone. It also supports SGLang, another open source inference server, in production. TensorRT-LLM integration is coming soon. Every node needs a shared cache backend. The setup:
  >
  > - Run vLLM with LMCache enabled on every node in the pool
  > - Point all nodes at the same shared cache backend
  > - Serve requests that repeat a long system prompt, not one-off prompts
  > - L...

- [2026-11-07 · Posted] [You are renting a GPU from a data center you've never seen. Before...](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/spheron_you-are-renting-a-gpu-from-a-data-center-activity-7524692293019127809-0Xi3)
  > You are renting a GPU from a data center you've never seen. Before you upload a model weight, one question matters more than price: can the people who run that rack read what you put on it?
  >
  > At Spheron, we worked with a team that couldn't expose inference data to anyone, including us. The GPU was rented, and the data center was run by a partner. So where does trust sit?
  >
  > NVIDIA TEE, short for trusted execution environment, answers the first part. Turn it on for an H200 and it encrypts the GPU's memory and isolates your workload from the host. The operator managing that server can't read your model weights or inputs while the job runs.
  >
  > A chip cannot vet a building. The GPU sits inside a physical facility. TEE doesn't check who holds a badge to that room or how secure it is. That's a separate guarantee: Tier 3+ certification, the standard every partner must meet.
  >
  > Two guarantees, not one. Before you trust a TEE-enabled node, check these:
  >
  > - Confirm TEE is enabled on the node, not jus...

- [2026-11-06 · Posted] [Two teams quantize the same model to 4-bit. Same weights, same GPU...](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/spheron_two-teams-quantize-the-same-model-to-4-bit-activity-7524329637477421056-oQ3L)
  > Two teams quantize the same model to 4-bit. Same weights, same GPU, same framework. One team serves 741 tokens a second. The other serves 68.
  >
  > Quantization shrinks a model's weights so they take less memory and run faster. It is natural to assume that same format means same speed everywhere it runs.
  >
  > That is wrong here: the precision is identical. What differs is the kernel, the actual code that runs the math on the GPU.
  >
  > Run AWQ on Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct using an H200 GPU. Swap only the kernel and the results split apart:
  >
  > - AWQ with the Marlin kernel: 741 tokens/s
  > - vLLM's default AWQ kernel: 68 tokens/s
  >
  > That is a 10.9x gap on the exact same quantized model. The weights did not change, only the code that executes them did.
  >
  > Cost follows throughput. The Marlin kernel brings cost per million output tokens down from about $19.61 to $1.80.
  >
  > Pick the format for memory savings and the kernel for speed. Treat them as one decision and you will ship a config that quietly costs 10x more than...
